steps.title: How JAK2 causes PV
nodes: JAK2 V617F mutation in a marrow stem cell
Red cells made without needing EPO
Kidney senses plenty of oxygen → EPO falls
Raised red cell mass, often with high WCC and platelets

steps.lead: Michael's red cells grow **without EPO**, so his kidneys switch EPO off. In COPD the opposite happens: hypoxia drives EPO up.
Michael's haematocrit of 0.58 makes his blood **viscous**, slowing the microcirculation: hence his headaches and clot risk.
Venesection lowers Michael's **red cell mass** and viscosity, but the JAK2 clone keeps making cells, so it is ongoing.
Michael's shower itch is **histamine** release from abnormal mast cells and basophils triggered by warm water.

steps.q: Why does Michael need lifelong follow-up even when his counts are controlled?
o: Risk of progression to myelofibrosis or AML
steps.r: Long-standing PV can enter a **spent phase**: myelofibrosis or, rarely, AML.

steps.lead: Years on, Michael's PV may enter a **spent phase**: falling counts, a bigger spleen, then myelofibrosis or rarely AML.

mcq.r: **OSA** causes nocturnal hypoxia and raises EPO; COPD, smoking and altitude do the same.

mcq.q: What is the serum EPO in polycythaemia vera?
mcq.r: **Low**: the clone grows without EPO, so it is suppressed. Raised EPO means secondary.

mcq.q: Why is EPO raised in secondary polycythaemia?
mcq.r: **Hypoxia** (or an EPO-producing tumour) drives a compensatory rise in EPO.

glossary.polycythaemia: An abnormally increased red cell mass, raising the haemoglobin and haematocrit.
glossary.polycythaemia vera: A JAK2-driven bone marrow cancer that overproduces red cells, often with white cells and platelets.
glossary.secondary polycythaemia: Raised red cells driven by raised EPO, from hypoxia or an EPO-producing tumour.
glossary.myeloproliferative: Describes clonal marrow disorders that overproduce one or more blood cell lines.
glossary.JAK2: A signalling enzyme; the V617F mutation switches it on permanently in PV.
glossary.JAK2 V617F: The point mutation in JAK2 found in almost all PV and many ET and myelofibrosis cases.
glossary.JAK-STAT: A signalling pathway that tells marrow cells to grow; always on in PV.
glossary.EPO: Erythropoietin: a kidney hormone that drives red cell production.
glossary.erythropoietin: A kidney hormone that drives red cell production; low in PV, raised in secondary polycythaemia.
glossary.erythrocytosis: An increase in red blood cells.
glossary.haematocrit: The proportion of blood volume made up of red cells; target below 0.45 in PV.
glossary.viscosity: How thick and sticky the blood is; higher viscosity slows flow and causes clots.
glossary.hyperviscosity: Blood so thick that flow slows, causing headache, visual upset and clots.
glossary.aquagenic pruritus: Itching after contact with water, especially a hot bath; characteristic of PV.
glossary.plethora: A ruddy, red complexion from excess red cells.
glossary.plethoric: Having a ruddy, red complexion from excess red cells.
glossary.erythromelalgia: Burning pain and redness of the hands and feet.
glossary.splenomegaly: An enlarged spleen, felt as a mass in the left upper quadrant.
glossary.Budd-Chiari syndrome: Hepatic vein thrombosis causing RUQ pain, hepatomegaly and ascites.
glossary.venesection: Removing blood from a vein to lower the red cell mass.
glossary.hydroxycarbamide: An oral cytoreductive drug that inhibits ribonucleotide reductase to lower blood counts.
glossary.cytoreductive therapy: Drugs that lower blood cell production in the marrow.
glossary.ribonucleotide reductase: The enzyme that makes DNA building blocks; blocked by hydroxycarbamide.
glossary.aspirin: An antiplatelet drug given at 75 mg daily in PV to reduce clots.
glossary.OSA: Obstructive sleep apnoea: repeated airway collapse in sleep causing night-time hypoxia.
glossary.CPAP: Continuous positive airway pressure: a mask that keeps the airway open in OSA.
glossary.COPD: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease; chronic hypoxia can cause secondary polycythaemia.
glossary.anabolic steroids: Testosterone-like drugs used in bodybuilding; they raise red cell production.
glossary.cyanotic heart disease: Congenital heart defects that mix deoxygenated blood into the systemic circulation.
glossary.myelofibrosis: Scarring of the bone marrow, causing anaemia, a large spleen and teardrop cells.
glossary.spent phase: Late PV when the marrow scars and counts fall, progressing to myelofibrosis.
glossary.AML: Acute myeloid leukaemia: a rare late transformation of PV.
glossary.gout: Painful joint inflammation from urate crystals; urate rises with high cell turnover.
glossary.urate: A breakdown product of cell DNA; raised when cell turnover is high.
glossary.histamine: A chemical released by mast cells and basophils that causes itching.
glossary.BCR-ABL: The Philadelphia chromosome fusion gene of chronic myeloid leukaemia, not PV.

technique.stem: A 64 year old man has 3 months of headaches and itching after a hot bath. He has never smoked. He has a ruddy complexion and a mass palpable in the left upper quadrant. His pulse rate is 76 bpm, BP 152/90 mmHg and oxygen saturation 98% breathing air.
technique.q: Which is the most likely diagnosis?

steps.x: A diagnosis question with a raised Hb: primary or secondary, and which MPN.
**Aquagenic pruritus**, plethora, splenomegaly, normal sats and no smoking: no hypoxic cause. The **Hb** is the dominant rise.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: **Polycythaemia vera**.

elim: CML gives a very high WCC with a left shift, massive spleen and BCR-ABL, not a dominant Hb rise.
ET is a platelet disorder; the Hb would be normal.
Myelofibrosis causes anaemia, not a raised Hb.
Secondary polycythaemia has normal WCC and platelets, no itch and no spleen.

steps.x: **C. Polycythaemia vera.** Rule: raised Hb + bath itch + spleen + normal sats = PV.

technique.stem: A 59 year old woman has a haemoglobin of 186 g/L found on a routine blood test. She has occasional headaches. She has never smoked, does not snore and her oxygen saturation is 98% breathing air. Her pulse rate is 72 bpm and BP 138/84 mmHg. A JAK2 mutation screen has been sent.
technique.q: Which other result would most support polycythaemia vera?

steps.x: Which result separates PV from secondary polycythaemia.
Raised Hb with **no hypoxic cause**: PV is likely.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: PV clone grows without EPO, so **EPO is low**.

elim: PV usually raises, not lowers, the white cell count.
Splenomegaly supports PV; a normal spleen does not.
Raised EPO points to secondary polycythaemia.
Ferritin is often low in PV as iron is used for red cells.

steps.x: **A. Low EPO.** Rule: low EPO = PV; raised EPO = secondary.

technique.stem: A 55 year old man has polycythaemia vera confirmed by a positive JAK2 V617F mutation. He has had no thrombosis. His pulse rate is 80 bpm and BP 136/84 mmHg.
technique.q: Which is the most appropriate initial management?

steps.x: First-line treatment of PV.
Low-risk PV with a haematocrit of 0.56.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: **Venesection** to a haematocrit **below 0.45**, plus aspirin 75 mg.

elim: Hydroxycarbamide is added for high-risk disease (older or previous thrombosis).
Imatinib is for CML (BCR-ABL).
Splenectomy is not a treatment for PV.
Warfarin does not lower the count and is not routine in PV.

steps.x: **D. Venesection to Hct below 0.45.** Rule: PV = venesect + aspirin; hydroxycarbamide if high risk.

technique.stem: A 70 year old woman with polycythaemia vera has a haematocrit of 0.60. She has headaches and blurred vision and is found to have a deep vein thrombosis of the left leg. Her pulse rate is 84 bpm and BP 150/88 mmHg.
technique.q: Which is the most likely mechanism of her thrombosis?

steps.x: Mechanism of thrombosis in polycythaemia.
Very high haematocrit with **hyperviscosity symptoms** and a clot.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: Raised red cell mass → **increased viscosity** → impaired flow → thrombosis.

elim: Nothing suggests an inherited thrombophilia.
She has had no surgery.
PV usually raises platelets; a low count causes bleeding, not clots.
Vitamin K excess is not a recognised cause of thrombosis.

steps.x: **C. Increased whole blood viscosity.** Rule: more red cells = thicker blood = clots.

practice.stem: A 68 year old woman has 6 months of itching after showers, headaches and burning pain in her feet. She has never smoked. Her face is red and her spleen is palpable. Her pulse rate is 78 bpm, BP 148/88 mmHg and oxygen saturation 97% breathing air.
practice.q: Which is the most likely diagnosis?
practice.e: Aquagenic pruritus, erythromelalgia, plethora, splenomegaly and a dominant Hb rise with raised WCC and platelets is PV. Secondary polycythaemia has normal WCC and platelets and no spleen.

steps.x: Diagnosis of a raised Hb.
**Aquagenic pruritus**, **erythromelalgia**, plethora, splenomegaly, no hypoxic cause.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: **Polycythaemia vera**.

elim: CML has a very high WCC with a left shift, not a dominant Hb rise.
ET does not raise the Hb.
Myelofibrosis causes anaemia.
Secondary polycythaemia has normal WCC and platelets and no splenomegaly.

steps.x: **C. Polycythaemia vera.**

practice.stem: A 52 year old man has morning headaches and daytime sleepiness. His wife says he snores loudly and stops breathing at night. His BMI is 41 kg/m². His pulse rate is 84 bpm, BP 154/96 mmHg and oxygen saturation 94% breathing air. His spleen is not palpable.
practice.q: Which is the most likely diagnosis?
practice.e: Obstructive sleep apnoea causes night-time hypoxia, raising EPO and the Hb: secondary polycythaemia. PV would have a low EPO and usually raised WCC and platelets.

steps.x: Diagnosis of a raised Hb: check EPO and the other lines.

clues: snores loudly and stops breathing at night
steps.x: **OSA** in obesity, normal WCC and platelets, **raised EPO**.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: Hypoxia-driven: **secondary polycythaemia**.

elim: CML raises the white count.
Dehydration (relative polycythaemia) would not raise the EPO.
ET raises platelets; his are normal.
PV has low EPO, and usually high WCC, platelets and a spleen.

steps.x: **E. Secondary polycythaemia.** Rule: raised EPO + hypoxic cause = secondary.

practice.stem: A 29 year old man has a haemoglobin of 190 g/L on a blood test for his gym membership. He trains daily and is preparing for a bodybuilding competition. He does not smoke or snore. His BMI is 27 kg/m². His oxygen saturation is 99% breathing air. His white cell count and platelet count are normal and the JAK2 mutation screen is negative.
practice.q: Which is the most likely cause of his raised haemoglobin?
practice.e: Anabolic steroids stimulate red cell production and are a recognised cause of secondary polycythaemia in a young bodybuilder. Normal sats and no snoring make hypoxic causes unlikely.

steps.x: Cause of a secondary polycythaemia.
Young bodybuilder, no hypoxia, JAK2 negative.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: **Anabolic steroids**.

elim: Nothing in the stem mentions altitude.
PV is rare at 29 and he has no other features.
He does not snore and his BMI is only 27.
Renal cell carcinoma is unlikely at 29 without haematuria or a mass.

steps.x: **A. Anabolic steroid use.** Rule: young bodybuilder + raised Hb = ask about steroids.

practice.stem: A 61 year old woman with polycythaemia vera has 2 weeks of right upper quadrant pain and increasing abdominal swelling. Her liver is enlarged and tender and there is shifting dullness. Her pulse rate is 96 bpm, BP 118/74 mmHg and temperature 36.9°C.
practice.q: Which is the most likely diagnosis?
practice.e: PV is the commonest cause of Budd-Chiari syndrome (hepatic vein thrombosis): RUQ pain, tender hepatomegaly and ascites. Cholecystitis would cause fever and no ascites.

steps.x: A complication of PV in the liver.
**PV** + RUQ pain + tender hepatomegaly + **ascites**: classic triad.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: Hepatic vein thrombosis: **Budd-Chiari syndrome**.

elim: Cholecystitis causes fever and Murphy's sign, not ascites.
HCC usually arises in a cirrhotic liver with weight loss.
Hepatitis A has a viral prodrome and no link to PV.
Right heart failure gives a raised JVP and leg oedema.

steps.x: **B. Budd-Chiari syndrome.** Rule: PV + RUQ pain + ascites = Budd-Chiari.

practice.stem: A 66 year old man has polycythaemia vera newly diagnosed after a raised haemoglobin was found. He has headaches and a red face. His pulse rate is 74 bpm and BP 146/90 mmHg.
practice.q: Which is the most likely finding on abdominal examination?
practice.e: Splenomegaly (a LUQ mass) is a common finding in PV and helps distinguish it from secondary polycythaemia. Ascites would suggest Budd-Chiari, a complication.

steps.x: Most likely examination finding in PV.
Uncomplicated new PV.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: **Splenomegaly**.

elim: Ascites suggests Budd-Chiari, a complication, not the usual finding.
Caput medusae is portal hypertension in cirrhosis.
A palpable bladder is urinary retention.
A pulsatile mass is an aortic aneurysm.

steps.x: **E. Splenomegaly.** Rule: PV = LUQ mass; secondary polycythaemia = no spleen.

practice.stem: A 74 year old man has had polycythaemia vera for 15 years. He no longer needs venesection. Over 6 months he has become more tired and has early satiety. His spleen is now palpable to the umbilicus. A blood film shows teardrop-shaped red cells and no blasts.
practice.q: Which is the most likely explanation?
practice.e: Long-standing PV in a spent phase with falling counts, massive splenomegaly and teardrop cells has progressed to secondary myelofibrosis. AML would show blasts and a high WBC.

steps.x: What has happened to a long-standing PV.
**Spent phase**: counts falling, massive spleen, **dacrocytes**, no blasts.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: **Progression to myelofibrosis**.

elim: AML would show blasts and usually a high WBC.
Hydroxycarbamide toxicity lowers counts but does not enlarge the spleen or make teardrop cells.
He no longer has venesection, and iron deficiency does not cause massive splenomegaly.
Splenic infarction causes acute LUQ pain.

steps.x: **D. Progression to myelofibrosis.** Rule: old PV + falling counts + teardrop cells = spent phase.

practice.stem: A 63 year old woman has headaches and itching after hot baths. She has a plethoric face and a palpable spleen. She has never smoked. Her pulse rate is 80 bpm, BP 150/90 mmHg and oxygen saturation 98% breathing air.
practice.q: Which is the most appropriate diagnostic investigation?
practice.e: The JAK2 mutation screen is the most important diagnostic test for PV, alongside FBC and EPO. Bone marrow biopsy is not first.

steps.x: Diagnostic test for suspected PV.
Classic **PV** picture.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: **JAK2 mutation screen**.

elim: BCR-ABL is for CML.
Marrow biopsy is for unclear cases or myelofibrosis.
Ferritin does not diagnose PV.
Catecholamines are for phaeochromocytoma.

steps.x: **C. JAK2 mutation screen.** Rule: suspected PV = JAK2 first.

practice.stem: A 71 year old man with severe COPD has a haemoglobin of 186 g/L. He smokes 30 cigarettes a day. His pulse rate is 92 bpm, BP 138/80 mmHg and oxygen saturation 87% breathing air. His spleen is not palpable.
practice.q: Which is the most likely finding on further investigation?
practice.e: Chronic hypoxia from COPD and smoking drives a compensatory rise in EPO: secondary polycythaemia. Low EPO and JAK2 point to PV.

steps.x: Predict a test result in a raised Hb.
**Chronic hypoxia**, normal WCC and platelets, no spleen.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: Secondary polycythaemia: **raised EPO**.

elim: JAK2 is the PV mutation.
Low EPO means PV.
The Philadelphia chromosome is CML.
Teardrop cells mean myelofibrosis.

steps.x: **D. Raised EPO.** Rule: hypoxia = high EPO = secondary polycythaemia.

practice.stem: A 48 year old woman has polycythaemia vera. Her haematocrit has been brought below 0.45 by venesection. She has had no thrombosis and has no bleeding history. Her pulse rate is 72 bpm and BP 128/80 mmHg.
practice.q: Which drug should be added to reduce her thrombotic risk?
practice.e: Low-dose aspirin 75 mg is added in PV to reduce thrombosis. Hydroxycarbamide is for high-risk disease (older or previous thrombosis), which she is not.

steps.x: The add-on drug in PV.
Low-risk PV, counts controlled, platelets well below 1500.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: **Aspirin 75 mg** once daily.

elim: A DOAC is not routine in PV without a VTE.
Clopidogrel is not the standard antiplatelet in PV.
Hydroxycarbamide is for high-risk disease.
Warfarin is not routine and raises bleeding risk.

steps.x: **B. Aspirin 75 mg.** Rule: PV = venesection + low-dose aspirin.

practice.stem: A 50 year old man has secondary polycythaemia. Sleep studies confirm severe obstructive sleep apnoea. His BMI is 39 kg/m². His pulse rate is 82 bpm and BP 150/94 mmHg. The JAK2 mutation screen is negative.
practice.q: Which is the most appropriate management?
practice.e: Secondary polycythaemia is treated by fixing the cause: CPAP corrects night-time hypoxia from OSA, so EPO and Hb fall. Hydroxycarbamide is for PV.

steps.x: Management of secondary polycythaemia.
The cause is **OSA**.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: Treat the cause: **CPAP**.

elim: Aspirin does not remove the hypoxic drive.
Hydroxycarbamide is cytoreduction for PV.
Imatinib is for CML.
Splenectomy has no role.

steps.x: **B. CPAP.** Rule: secondary polycythaemia = treat the cause.

practice.stem: A 76 year old man with polycythaemia vera had an ischaemic stroke 1 year ago. He has needed venesection every 2 weeks to control his haematocrit and is finding it hard to tolerate. His pulse rate is 78 bpm and BP 140/84 mmHg.
practice.q: Which is the most appropriate additional treatment?
practice.e: Older age and previous thrombosis make this high-risk PV: add cytoreduction with hydroxycarbamide, which inhibits ribonucleotide reductase. Imatinib is for CML.

steps.x: Treatment for uncontrolled, high-risk PV.
**Elderly**, previous **thrombosis**, poorly controlled with venesection.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: Cytoreduction: **hydroxycarbamide**.

elim: Allopurinol treats gout, not the counts.
Transplant is not used for PV at his age.
Imatinib targets BCR-ABL in CML.
Splenectomy does not control PV.

steps.x: **C. Hydroxycarbamide.** Rule: high-risk PV = add hydroxycarbamide.

practice.stem: A 60 year old man has polycythaemia vera. His haemoglobin is 195 g/L. His serum erythropoietin is low and a JAK2 V617F mutation is detected.
practice.q: Which is the most likely mechanism of his low erythropoietin?
o: EPO-independent red cell production suppressing EPO
practice.e: The JAK2 V617F clone makes red cells without needing EPO; the raised red cell mass then suppresses renal EPO production. Hypoxia would raise EPO.

steps.x: Mechanism of a test result in PV.
**Constitutive JAK-STAT signalling** drives red cells independently of EPO.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: Autonomous production → negative feedback → **EPO suppressed**.

elim: CKD causes anaemia, not a Hb of 195.
Hypoxia raises EPO.
Iron deficiency does not lower EPO.
The spleen does not destroy EPO.

steps.x: **B. EPO-independent production suppressing EPO.** Rule: PV = autonomous clone, low EPO.
